questions.question: Which country has imposed a 13% value-added tax on condoms and contraceptive drugs from January 1, 2026, as part of efforts to boost its declining birth rate?
questions.questionHtml: Which country has imposed a 13% value-added tax on condoms and contraceptive drugs from January 1, 2026, as part of efforts to boost its declining birth rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is China.

In News

  • China removed a three-decade-old tax exemption on condoms and contraceptive drugs to encourage higher birth rates.

Key Points

  • China imposed a 13% value-added tax on condoms and contraceptive pills from January 1, 2026.
  • The tax exemption had been in place for nearly 30 years.
  • The move aims to address China’s declining birth rate.
  • China’s population fell for the third consecutive year in 2024.

Additional Information

  • Demographic Context
    • China has experienced falling birth rates for decades.
    • Decline attributed to the former one-child policy, urbanisation and rising living costs.
    • High childcare and education expenses discourage family formation.
  • Government Measures
    • Childcare subsidies exempted from personal income tax.
    • Annual childcare subsidy introduced in 2024.
    • Promotion of positive marriage and childbearing attitudes through policy messaging.
  • Policy Significance
    • Reflects China’s shift towards fertility-friendly economic policies.
    • Part of broader efforts announced at the Central Economic Work Conference.
    • Aims to stabilise population decline in the long term.

questions.question: Which country has officially legalised cryptocurrency mining and exchanges in 2026 by introducing a licensing framework overseen by its central bank?
questions.questionHtml: Which country has officially legalised cryptocurrency mining and exchanges in 2026 by introducing a licensing framework overseen by its central bank?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Turkmenistan.

In News

  • Turkmenistan has legalised cryptocurrency mining and exchanges as part of an economic policy shift.

Key Points

  • Turkmenistan legalised crypto mining and exchanges through legislation signed in January 2026.
  • The law establishes a licensing system regulated by the country’s central bank.
  • Cryptocurrencies are regulated as virtual assets under civil law.
  • Digital currencies are not recognised as legal tender or a means of payment.

Additional Information

  • Economic Context
    • Turkmenistan is a gas-dependent economy with vast natural gas reserves.
    • China is the largest importer of Turkmen gas.
    • The country is exploring diversification through digital economy reforms.
  • Governance and Reform
    • Legislation signed by President Serdar Berdimuhamedov.
    • Marks a rare economic liberalisation in one of the world’s most isolated nations.
    • Part of broader steps including e-visa introduction and digital governance.
  • Cryptocurrency Regulation
    • Crypto activities permitted under a licensing framework.
    • Exchanges supervised by the central bank.
    • Use of crypto as currency or security remains prohibited.

questions.question: Cyprus assumed the rotating presidency of the European Union for a six-month term beginning in which city?
questions.questionHtml: Cyprus assumed the rotating presidency of the European Union for a six-month term beginning in which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nicosia.

In News

  • Cyprus assumed the rotating presidency of the European Union with a high-level meeting held in Nicosia.

Key Points

  • This is the second time Cyprus has held the EU Council presidency since joining the EU in 2004.
  • The inauguration meeting in Nicosia was attended by Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa.
  • Cyprus highlighted its role as a bridge between Europe and the Middle East, with regional leaders attending the ceremony.
  • The presidency focuses on strengthening EU autonomy and advancing European integration amid global challenges.

Additional Information

  • Zelenskiy’s participation signalled continued EU support for Ukraine as the Russia-Ukraine war enters its fourth year.
  • Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides emphasised EU strategic autonomy as a key priority of the presidency.

questions.question: In March 2026, how many nations have formed a global coalition to secure maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz following regional tensions?
questions.questionHtml: In March 2026, how many nations have formed a global coalition to secure maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz following regional tensions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 22.

In News

  • A coalition of 22 nations, led by the UAE, Bahrain, and Western powers, has been formed to secure the Strait of Hormuz.

Key Points

  • Context: The coalition is a response to Iranian threats to target vessels in the strait following regional strikes in late February 2026.
  • Signatories: The group includes major economies like the UK, France, Germany, Japan, Canada, and South Korea.
  • Energy Impact: The Strait of Hormuz is a vital artery where approximately 20 million barrels of oil pass daily.
  • Legal Basis: The coalition cited the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to emphasize that freedom of navigation is non-negotiable.
  • Economic Action: The group welcomed the International Energy Agency (IEA) decision to release strategic petroleum reserves to stabilize the market.

Geographical Importance

  • Strait of Hormuz
    • It is a narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. It is considered the world's most important oil chokepoint.
  • UNCLOS
    • The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea is an international agreement that establishes a legal framework for all marine and maritime activities.

questions.question: Which country has approved the world's first commercial stem-cell therapies for Parkinson's and heart failure?
questions.questionHtml: Which country has approved the world's first commercial stem-cell therapies for Parkinson's and heart failure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Japan.

In News

  • Japan has officially approved the first commercial medical products derived from induced Pluripotent Stem (iPS) cells for treating Parkinson’s and heart failure.

Key Points

  • The Parkinson’s treatment, named Amchepry, replaces lost dopamine-producing cells in the brain using stem-cell precursors.
  • The heart failure treatment, ReHeart, consists of heart muscle sheets designed to form new blood vessels and restore function.
  • These breakthroughs are based on the Nobel Prize-winning research of Shinya Yamanaka (2012), who discovered how to revert mature cells to a pluripotent state.
  • Both therapies have received provisional licenses and are expected to be clinically available by Summer 2026.

Additional Information

  • iPS Cells
    • Induced Pluripotent Stem cells are adult cells that have been genetically reprogrammed to an embryonic stem cell-like state.
  • Shinya Yamanaka
    • A Japanese scientist who won the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery that mature cells can be reprogrammed to become pluripotent.
  • Dopamine
    • A neurotransmitter in the brain; the loss of dopamine-producing cells is the primary cause of Parkinson's disease symptoms.
  • Provisional License
    • A conditional approval that allows earlier access to innovative treatments while long-term data continues to be collected.

questions.question: The national emergency declared by US President Donald Trump regarding Venezuelan funds was aimed at
questions.questionHtml: The national emergency declared by US President Donald Trump regarding Venezuelan funds was aimed at

options.text: Allowing private creditors to recover debts
options.html: Allowing private creditors to recover debts

options.text: Preventing judicial seizure of Venezuelan sovereign funds
options.html: Preventing judicial seizure of Venezuelan sovereign funds

options.text: Transferring Venezuelan assets to international courts
options.html: Transferring Venezuelan assets to international courts

options.text: Permitting free market trading of Venezuelan resources
options.html: Permitting free market trading of Venezuelan resources

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Preventing judicial seizure of Venezuelan sovereign funds.

In News

  • US President Donald Trump declared a national emergency to block courts and creditors from seizing Venezuelan government funds held in the United States.

Key Points

  • The executive order blocks judicial attachment, judgment, lien, or garnishment of Venezuelan funds.
  • Such actions were termed a threat to US national security and foreign policy.
  • The protected funds are classified as Foreign Government Deposit Funds.
  • These funds are derived from the sale of natural resources and diluents to the Venezuelan government.

Additional Information

  • Sovereign Property – The funds are explicitly recognised as the sovereign assets of Venezuela, not property of private entities or judgment creditors.
  • Judicial Protection – Any legal action against these funds is prohibited unless licensed by the US administration.
  • Custodial Role of the US – The US government will hold the funds in a custodial and governmental capacity, not as a market participant.
  • Foreign Government Deposit Funds – Refers to state-owned financial assets derived from natural resource transactions and held within US jurisdiction.

questions.question: The United States has completed its withdrawal from the World Health Organization, ending its membership for the first time since which year?
questions.questionHtml: The United States has completed its withdrawal from the World Health Organization, ending its membership for the first time since which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1948.

In News

  • The United States has ended its membership in the World Health Organization for the first time since the organization was established in 1948.

Key Points

  • The World Health Organization was founded in 1948, with the United States as a founding member.
  • The U.S. announced its plan to leave the WHO on January 20, 2025.
  • The withdrawal process lasted one year and involved halting funding and withdrawing personnel.
  • The decision was taken citing WHO’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic and lack of institutional reforms.

Additional Information

  • World Health Organization
    • A specialized agency of the United Nations established in 1948.
    • Coordinates international efforts on disease control and public health emergencies.
  • United States and WHO
    • The U.S. was historically one of the largest contributors to the WHO.
    • The withdrawal marks a significant shift in global health cooperation.
  • Global Health Governance
    • Refers to international coordination to address global health challenges.
    • Has faced scrutiny following the COVID-19 pandemic.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases has Chile recently become the first country in the Americas to be officially verified by the WHO for eliminating as a public health problem?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following diseases has Chile recently become the first country in the Americas to be officially verified by the WHO for eliminating as a public health problem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Leprosy.

In News

  • In 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) announced that Chile is the first country in the Americas to achieve the elimination of leprosy as a public health problem.

Key Points

  • Chile is only the 4th country globally to receive this specific official WHO verification for leprosy elimination.
  • The elimination status is defined as reaching a prevalence rate of less than 1 case per 10,000 population at the national level.
  • Key factors for this success included high Multidrug Therapy (MDT) coverage and effective prevention of physical disabilities.
  • The country maintained a high treatment completion rate of over 95% and a very low proportion of cases among children.

Additional Information

  • Leprosy (Hansen’s Disease)
    • Causative Agent - A slow-growing bacterium called Mycobacterium leprae.
    • Impact - It primarily affects the skin, nerves, upper respiratory tract, and eyes. If left untreated, it can cause permanent damage.
  • Global Leprosy Strategy
    • Goal - The WHO's Global Leprosy Strategy (2021–2030) aims for "Towards Zero Leprosy," focusing on zero infection, zero disease, and zero stigma.
  • Multidrug Therapy (MDT)
    • Nature - A combination of three antibiotics (Dapsone, Rifampicin, and Clofazimine) which has been the gold standard for curing leprosy since the 1980s.

questions.question: The Senkaku Islands dispute involves which two countries?
questions.questionHtml: The Senkaku Islands dispute involves which two countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Japan and China.

Key Points

  • The Senkaku Islands dispute involves two countries: Japan and China. These islands are located in the East China Sea.
  • The Senkaku Islands, known as Diaoyu Islands in China, are uninhabited but strategically important due to their location and potential reserves of oil and gas.
  • Japan claims sovereignty over the islands based on their annexation in 1895 after defeating China in the First Sino-Japanese War.
  • China argues that the islands have been a part of its territory since ancient times, citing historical documents and maps from the Ming Dynasty.
  • The dispute escalated significantly after Japan purchased three of the islands from private owners in 2012, prompting protests and strong objections from China.
  • The islands are situated near rich fishing grounds and are also strategically important for controlling sea lanes in the region.

Additional Information

  • Historical Background:
    • Japan formally annexed the islands in 1895 after the Treaty of Shimonoseki, which ended the First Sino-Japanese War.
    • China claims that the islands have been part of its territory since the Ming Dynasty (1368–1644).
    • After World War II, the islands were administered by the United States under the San Francisco Peace Treaty in 1951 and returned to Japan in 1972.
  • Geopolitical Importance:
    • The islands are located in the East China Sea, near major shipping lanes, making them strategically vital for maritime security.
    • The surrounding waters are rich in marine resources, especially fish, and believed to contain oil and natural gas reserves.
    • The dispute has implications for regional stability, particularly involving China-Japan relations and the role of the United States as an ally of Japan.
  • Current Status:
    • Japan currently administers the islands, but China continues to assert its claim, often sending patrol ships and aircraft near the islands.
    • The dispute has led to diplomatic tensions, protests, and occasional confrontations between the two nations.
    • Efforts at negotiation have been sporadic, with each side maintaining their respective positions.
  • International Law:
    • The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) allows nations to claim Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs), which has fueled the dispute over the islands.
    • China often cites historical sovereignty, while Japan points to effective control under international law.
    • Despite claims, international arbitration has not resolved the dispute due to the unwillingness of the involved parties to submit the matter to international courts.

Important Points

  • Role of the United States:
    • The United States maintains a neutral stance on sovereignty but recognizes Japan's administrative control of the islands.
    • Under the US-Japan Security Treaty, the United States is obligated to defend Japan in case of an armed attack on the islands.
    • This has added a layer of complexity to the dispute, as China views US involvement as interference.
  • Regional Implications:
    • The dispute is part of broader territorial disagreements in the region, including China's claims in the South China Sea.
    • It is closely monitored by neighboring countries and international organizations due to its potential impact on regional security and trade.
  • Efforts at Resolution:
    • Both nations have occasionally engaged in dialogue, but mutual distrust has hindered substantial progress.
    • Regional organizations like ASEAN have called for peaceful resolution and adherence to international law.
    • Track II diplomacy and academic exchanges have been suggested to ease tensions and improve mutual understanding.

questions.question: Guatemala recently declared a 30-day nationwide state of emergency amid deadly gang violence. What is the name of Guatemala’s currency?
questions.questionHtml: Guatemala recently declared a 30-day nationwide state of emergency amid deadly gang violence. What is the name of Guatemala’s currency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Guatemalan Quetzal.

  • Guatemalan Quetzal is correct as it is the official currency of Guatemala, used for all domestic and international transactions.
  • Guatemalan Peso is incorrect because Guatemala does not use the peso; it is used by countries like Mexico and Argentina.
  • Central American Dollar is incorrect as no such official currency exists in the region.
  • Lempira is incorrect because it is the official currency of Honduras, not Guatemala.

In News

  • Guatemala declared a 30-day nationwide state of emergency in January 2026 following deadly gang violence.

Key Points

  • Official Currency: The Guatemalan Quetzal is the legal tender of Guatemala.
  • Currency Code: It is denoted by the ISO code GTQ.
  • Subdivision: One Quetzal is subdivided into 100 centavos.
  • Economic Role: The currency plays a vital role in Guatemala’s domestic economy and trade.

Additional Information

  • Quetzal: Named after the resplendent quetzal bird, a national symbol of Guatemala representing liberty.
  • Introduced: The Guatemalan Quetzal was introduced in 1925.
  • Capital City: Guatemala City is the capital and financial hub of the country.

Important Points

  • Gang Violence Context: The emergency was declared due to coordinated gang attacks involving MS-13 and Barrio 18.
  • Government Measures: The state of emergency allows expanded arrest powers to restore public order.
